For every version of an artifact carried on the evidence hop, `device_id` remains present with its v1 meaning.
`local_seq` remains present with its v1 meaning on delivery envelopes;
`from_seq` and `to_seq` remain present with their v1 meanings on delivery receipts.
A later version may add fields but MUST NOT repurpose or remove these routing fields.

`device_id` is a string of 1 to 128 Unicode scalar values, none of them a control character (general category `Cc`), a character with the Unicode `White_Space` property, `/`, `+`, or `#`, as a carriage topic segment requires;
`local_seq`, `from_seq` and `to_seq` are integers of at least 1.
`anchor_epoch_id` remains present with its v1 meaning on anchor registrations, delivery envelopes and checkpoints.
Its v1 domain is `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
`anchor_epoch_id` is part of the stable routing projection for every carried device artifact.
The courier may read it only to bind queue entries to a verified epoch-scoped stop projection.
It MUST NOT use it to infer confirmation, validity, ordering, authority state or artifact acceptance.
The stop projection is defined in [evidence-transport/v2.md](../evidence-transport/v2.md).
A courier reads only this projection and never interprets an artifact's version.

It reads each routing field by its exact member name, compared byte for byte: a member whose name differs only in letter case is not that field, and an artifact that names any member twice is not routable.
The projection holds for evidence dispositions as for every other carried artifact.
[`vectors/routing-projection-v2.json`](vectors/routing-projection-v2.json) fixes it, and `scripts/check-evidence-routing-projection-vectors` holds the corpus to this section.
